turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: Hi Maya, I'm Wren. I'm here to help you practice and stay steady through your job search. How are you feeling as we get started?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Hey Wren. A little overwhelmed, to be honest. I finished school in May and I'm aiming for tech sales, specifically business development roles at SaaS companies, so it's a lot of applying right now.

turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: That transition is a big lift. What is one experience you are most eager to talk about in interviews?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Probably something from my student consulting club. I actually led a group of five people on a project for a nonprofit, and we managed to cut down their donor churn by twelve percent.

turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: Leading a team to a twelve percent drop is a concrete result. What was the change you made that kept those donors around?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Well, we realized they weren't getting touched after the first donation. So we built an outreach sequence with automated check-ins and personal thank-you calls, which kept them engaged.

turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: That lines up directly with what outbound reps do. How do you feel when you share that story in front of people?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: If it's just one person, I feel pretty confident and normal. It flows well enough when it's a one-on-one chat.

turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: One-on-one conversation suits you. What format feels harder to handle?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Panel interviews make me so nervous. Whenever there are more than two people in the room listening to me, my mind just goes completely blank.

turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: Having multiple eyes on you raises the stakes fast. When your mind blanks out, what happens next?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I usually freeze for a second, panic, and then start rambling because silence feels awful. Then I totally lose the point I was trying to make.

turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: That silence can feel loud, but taking a breath gives you room to think. Would you like to practice handling a panel setup together soon?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yeah, that'd actually be really good. I definitely need to get comfortable with that pressure before real ones happen.

turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: We will build up to it together so it feels routine. Do you want to wrap up our check-in here for today?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yeah, let's call it here. Thanks, Wren, this was a nice start.
